facts.text: Jardine sits five miles northwest of Gardiner, accessible by unpaved Bear Gulch Road, a dirt route that can be rough when wet.
The town’s chief industry was a gold mine that produced over 4,400 kg of gold, 347,000 kg of tungsten, and 5.7 million kg of arsenic by 1943.
Gold was first discovered in Bear Gulch in 1866 when prospector Joe Brown found a gold‑quartz vein above what would become Gardiner.
Jardine sits in the Bear Gulch drainage of the Gallatin Range, close enough to Yellowstone’s gateway to benefit from tourism yet remote enough to keep a mining feel.
The tension between Jardine’s mining heritage and the Yellowstone ecosystem remains a defining characteristic of the town today.
Jardine’s historic ghost town is tucked away in Montana’s Garnet Mountains, where gold was discovered in 1865 by Bob and Joe Booth and Charles Hickey.
